title: A zebrafish tailfin injury assay protocol for quantifying immune cell migration and infiltration
protocol: Cross the transgenic zebrafish (with labeled immune cells – e.g., Tg(mpeg:GFP)) a day prior to collecting embryos.
Collect the zebrafish eggs from timed pairwise spawning tanks in the morning after the daylight period begins.
Place collected eggs in 100 mm petri dishes containing egg-water supplemented with methylene blue (100 μL per 1 L).
Incubate the embryos at 37°C for 6 hours.
Pour tank water through a fine metal mesh strainer to capture eggs.
Maintain captured eggs at 28°C in approximately 20 ml of system water in 100 mm plastic petri plates until unfertilized eggs can be identified and removed.
Sort fertilized embryos into fresh petri plates at a density of less than 50 embryos per plate.
Fill each dish with approximately 20 ml of fresh egg water.
Change to PTU-egg-water to prevent pigmentation of the fish.
Transfer larvae to a new petri dish containing PTU-egg-water supplemented with 0.01% Tricaine.
Sort transgenic larvae by epifluorescence using a dissecting microscope.
Align the larvae horizontally and dissect the distal tip of the tailfin with a sharp scalpel.
Transfer the larvae to fresh PTU-egg-water to wash out tricaine and revive.
Recover the larvae in a 28.5°C incubator for 6 hours post-injury.
Transfer the larvae to a freshly prepared 3% Formaldehyde solution in PEM buffer.
Incubate the larvae at 4°C for 16–18 hours.
As an alternative, transfer up to 6 larvae to 3% molten low-melting temperature agarose prepared in egg water + 0.01% Tricaine.
Transfer the larvae to coverslip-bottom 35 mm petri dishes and image on a confocal microscope for a time course of up to 12 hours.
Wash the larvae twice with PBS.
Incubate the larvae with PBS on an orbital shaker for 5 minutes per wash.
Permeabilize the larvae with PWDT for 20 minutes at 22°C–28°C.
Wash the larvae once with PWD.
Block non-specific antibody binding with PWDB containing 4% BSA for 30 minutes at 22°C–28°C.
Wash the larvae once with PWD.
Immunostain with primary antibodies by incubating at 4°C for 18 hours in a 1:250 dilution of Chicken anti-GFP antibody.
Wash the larvae three times with PWD.
Immunostain with secondary antibodies by incubating at 4°C for 18 hours in a 1:500 dilution of desired AlexaFluor labeled antibody.
Wash the larvae three times with PWD.
Mount the larvae on glass slides in an anti-fade mounting solution such as Vectashield.
Quantify manually the number of immune cells distal to the notochord and through to the injury site.
Perform statistical analysis to analyze differences in immune cell migration.
